text:
[LINT.1.1] An `Interval` value is a half-open range
`[start, end)` over one element type `T`:

```
Interval<T>: (start: T, end: T)
```

`T` is one of the types whose values `<` orders, and no other: `Int` and
`Float` ([LEXP.7.3]), `String` ([LSTR.3.2]), `Time`, `Date` and `Duration`
([LTIM.5]). `Interval<Time>` and `Interval<Date>` are the time windows
the rest of this document mostly speaks of; every rule here that does not name
an element type holds for all of them.

alloy.name: lint_1_1__instant
alloy.note: The element type as one set of atoms under util/ordering's total order, named `instant` for the time windows the document mostly speaks of. Nothing in the model reads anything of the type but `lt` / `lte` of that order, so every check holds for each of the clause's six element types alike -- Int and Float as one numeric type ([LINT.1.2]), String, Time, Date, Duration -- wherever `<` is a strict total order on the values. Not modelled: a Float NaN, on which `<` is not total; [LEXP.4.2] keeps one out of every slot, and whether one an expression computes may reach `..` is [LINT.2.2]'s question, not the algebra's.

alloy.name: lint_1_1__interval
alloy.note: A half-open `[start, end)` with `start <= end` over one element type, as the clause defines it; which type is the order's business, above.
